clue.text: Many tease girl about being a slowcoach

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole string of pieces is read from the end

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
to rag someone is to tease them
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a dawdling young woman, teasing her for lagging behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole run D + RAG + GAL (DRAGGAL) backwards. 'being a slowcoach' defines a person who is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dawdler who falls behind is a slowcoach, the British word for someone who moves too slowly.

clue.text: Panorama gets down to the point

parts.note: to land is to get down from the air
a cape is a headland or point

explanation.surface: A wide view stretches down to the headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad sweep of scenery viewed at once is a panorama.

clue.text: Suppressing comic business name in musical engagement

parts.note: a gag is a joke or piece of comic business

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for name inside the booking

parts.note: a gig is a booking for a musician

explanation.surface: A comedian's routine is silenced at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Gagging someone silences them, holding back or stifling what they would say.

clue.text: Large pieces of major road faulty in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle places the word for faulty inside the road

parts.note: an artery is a main road
ill can mean bad or faulty, as in ill-made

explanation.surface: Big chunks of a broken main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large pieces' means big guns, not chunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Big guns are called pieces, and heavy guns collectively form the artillery.

clue.text: Spots from above the eyes to the ears

definitions.text: Spots from above the eyes to the ears

parts.words: Spots from above the eyes to the ears
parts.note: the points over each letter i, and the short signals heard in Morse code

explanation.surface: Freckles spreading across a face from brow to ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyes' are the letter i, each with a point above it; to the ears, Morse code is points and dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Small round marks are spots, as on a lowercase i, and short Morse signals bear the same name.

clue.text: Side-effects of quarrel

explanation.surface: Collateral consequences of a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Radioactive debris and later consequences are both side-effects; to fall out with someone is to have a row.

clue.text: In place of locks in castles

parts.note: for can mean instead of, as in 'swap this for that'
tresses are locks of hair

explanation.surface: Hair replacing the locks in strongholds.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a fortified building or stronghold.

clue.text: The rope used to catch in windlass operation

indicators.note: in signals the answer is found inside the words windlass operation

explanation.surface: A line wound round a winch to hook something.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's noosed rope thrown to catch cattle.

clue.text: Crazy moronic character abroad

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of moronic go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: A mad foolish figure overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter, and 'abroad' makes it a Greek one.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter of the Greek alphabet is a foreign character.

clue.text: Suitable flower for the border?

parts.note: flower is read as something that flows, a river, and the border is that between England and Scotland

explanation.surface: Which bloom should go in the herbaceous border?
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' and 'border' paint gardening; the flower is a river that marks part of the Anglo-Scottish frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: The river forms much of the boundary between England and Scotland.

clue.text: "… All the world will be in love with ______" (R and J)

definitions.text: "… All the world will be in love with ______" (R and J)

parts.words: "… All the world will be in love with ______" (R and J)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Juliet's speech in Romeo and Juliet, where she wishes Romeo cut out in little stars

explanation.surface: A line from Romeo and Juliet with the last word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet says that Romeo, cut out in stars, will make 'all the world ... be in love with' the dark hours, and pay no worship to the garish sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word completes Shakespeare's line about the dark hours after sunset, when the stars shine.

clue.text: Revolver to use when approaching big game

definitions.text: Revolver to use when approaching big game

parts.words: Revolver to use when approaching big game
parts.note: not a gun for hunting large animals but a rotating gate that football fans push through on the way into a big match

explanation.surface: A hunter's pistol for stalking large animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' and 'big game' paint a safari with a handgun; the revolver is a rotating barrier and the game is a sports fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating barrier at a stadium entrance turns as each spectator goes in to watch the match.

clue.text: Protection for the prize

explanation.surface: Something guarding the trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrior's guard is a shield; many sports competitions award a shield as their trophy.

clue.text: Awful dream about our car, perhaps

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A nightmare involving our vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' shuffles DREAM and OUR; 'about' just links. 'car, perhaps' points to an armoured car, one kind of thing so described.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoured car is a steel-plated vehicle, so a car is an example of something with such plating.

clue.text: Stupid attendant in the lift

parts.note: dumb is slang for stupid
a waiter attends on diners

explanation.surface: A thick servant in the elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hoist for carrying food between floors is a lift.

clue.text: Glean new point of view

indicators.note: new suggests the word glean is remade in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Pick up a fresh perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges GLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular slant or standpoint on a matter is a point of view.

clue.text: Stars of University arts society comparatively unimportant

parts.note: the RSA is the Royal Society of Arts in London
minor means lesser or of small importance relative to others

explanation.surface: Celebrities of a college art club turn out to be small fry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like famous people, but it is a constellation, the Little Bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The Little Bear is a constellation, a group of stars that includes the Pole Star.

clue.text: Quite a long way overweight an important stage in life!

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a mile is quite a long distance
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Being well above one's weight is a landmark moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overweight' splits as over + weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A marker stone on a road, figuratively a significant event or landmark.

clue.text: Good customer takes advert out of The Lady as a rule

parts.note: a regular is a frequent, loyal customer

indicators.note: out of with takes means the advert is removed from the magazine name

parts.note: The Lady is a long-running British women's magazine

explanation.surface: A loyal reader removes an advert from a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lady is a British weekly magazine; 'takes ... out of' removes AD from LADY, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitually, usually, normally: all mean as a rule.

clue.text: Sweetheart — sweetheart in New York — clever and delightful!

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the abbreviation for New York

parts.note: jo is an old Scots word for a sweetheart
able means capable or clever

explanation.surface: Someone's darling in Manhattan is bright and charming.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Sweetheart' is read as sweet's heart, E; the second is JO, placed inside NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pleasing and delightful is a pleasure to experience.

clue.text: Woodwork put together on oriental lines

parts.note: to join is to put together
E for east, the Orient
RY is railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: Carpentry assembled along Eastern lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry of doors and fittings is joiners' work, or woodwork.

clue.text: Remaining false

explanation.surface: Staying put and telling untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left lying stays where it is, remaining; a lying statement is untrue or false.

clue.text: Train that is involved in dubious form of selling

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A rail service caught up in shady sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links. Inertia selling sends unrequested goods and charges unless they are returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia selling relies on a buyer's passivity to bill for unordered goods, a dubious sales practice.

clue.text: Unduly push artist the Italian, way…

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
il is Italian for the
a road is a way

explanation.surface: Pressure is applied to a painter, an Italian and a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into the next.
explanation.definitionFit: To force someone into something hastily or unfairly is to steamroller or push them through.

clue.text: Fleet attack includes first stage of Polaris

indicators.note: includes means the attack holds the other letter within it

parts.note: a raid is an attack

indicators.note: the first stage of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A naval attack involving the launch of a missile.
explanation.walkthrough: Polaris is a missile; its first stage is P.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift or fast.

clue.text: Soldiers with foreign terms of reference

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: Troops given instructions from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the scope of a task as defined by its terms of reference.

clue.text: … a person of distinction, too

parts.note: a swell is a fashionable or distinguished person

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a dignitary comes along too.
explanation.definitionFit: Also, in addition, besides: all mean too.

clue.text: Girl squeezing in at the entrance

indicators.note: squeezing in means the girl is pressed inside the other word

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A young woman squeezes through a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal entrance passage into a mine is an adit.

clue.text: Forestalled by boy, after English master starts in school

indicators.note: after puts the boy at the end of the other pieces
in puts the first pieces inside the word for a school

parts.note: a prep school is a preparatory school, shortened to prep

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of master is taken

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad beat others to it after a teacher began at school.
explanation.walkthrough: E and M (from 'master starts') go inside PREP to give PREEMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To pre-empt is to act first so as to prevent another's action, which is to forestall it.

clue.text: Ring to arouse true love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

indicators.note: arouse means stir up, so the letters of true are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A wedding band to stir up genuine affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arouse' stirs TRUE into UTER, placed after O; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: On an archery target the outermost ring is called the outer.

clue.text: Sun ages sailor

parts.note: days, as in 'in my day', means ages or eras
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Sunshine weathers an old seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning star, and poetically the sun itself, is called the day-star.

clue.text: Cutback in your old treatment

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the archaic word for your

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: A cutback in your traditional medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutback' splits as cut + back: PARE turned round gives ERAP, which goes inside THY.
explanation.definitionFit: A course of remedial care for an illness or condition is a form of treatment.
